rationale: Employees can see a weak rewrite instantly and just retry. A bad answer costs a few seconds, so cost per request dominates.
A wrong answer reaches a customer: a support ticket (~₹150) and some lost trust. Acceptable answers are fine, but errors must be rare.
Wrong numbers can propagate into reports, but analysts usually sanity-check results.
Broken code costs developer time to spot and fix. Code can be verified by tests, so a verify-then-escalate cascade is possible.
Wrong technical advice can waste days of engineering effort. Errors are expensive.
Learning content: an acceptable explanation does the job, and the learner can ask a follow-up.
Feeds real product decisions. A weaker analysis can cost far more than tokens, and volume is low, so the bar is the best available answer.
Huge free volume with no revenue per request. Acceptable advice keeps users engaged; cost must stay near zero.
Paying users expect the best coaching; weaker answers drive churn of a ₹499/month plan.
